subject: general
question: A cistern can be filled with water by a pipe in 10 hours, and it can be emptied by asecond pipe in 8 hours. If both the pipes are opened when the cistern is full, the time in which it will be emptied is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Time to empty = (**Filling time** × **Emptying time**) ÷ (**Emptying time** − **Filling time**)

Required time = (10 × 8) ÷ (10 − 8)

Required time = 80 ÷ 2 = 40 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe (A) = 10 hours

Emptying pipe (B) = 8 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 **Pipe** **Time (hr)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency (units/hr)**
 A (Filling) 10 40 units +4
 B (Emptying) 8 −5
⇒ Net efficiency of (A + B) = +4 − 5 = −1 unit/hr

⇒ Negative sign indicates the cistern is being emptied.

⇒ Time to empty full cistern = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time = 40 ÷ 1 = 40 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An **Inlet pipe** fills the tank (positive efficiency), while an **Outlet pipe** empties it (negative efficiency).

Net Work Done

If efficiency of the outlet pipe is greater than the inlet pipe, a full tank will always be **emptied**.

Total Work Assumption

Total capacity is usually taken as the **LCM** of time taken by individual pipes for easier calculations.</p
